subproblem.title: Graph coordinates, the rotated plane T_0 = q(R^n x {0}), and Hilbert-Schmidt norm basics
subproblem.statement: For all n, l >= 0 and every linear isometry q of R^(n+l) = Amb n l: write graphPoint(a, b) for the point of R^(n+l) whose first n coordinates are those of a in R^n and whose last l coordinates are those of b in R^l, T_0 := rotatedPlane q = q(horizontalPlane) with horizontalPlane = span{e_{castAdd l i} : i < n}, and P_{T_0} its orthogonal projection. Then (L1) graphPoint(a + a', b + b') = graphPoint(a, b) + graphPoint(a', b'); (L2) graphPoint(a - a', b - b') = graphPoint(a, b) - graphPoint(a', b'); (L3) graphPoint(t a, t b) = t graphPoint(a, b) for real t; (L4) |graphPoint(a, b)|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2; (L5) P_{T_0}(q(graphPoint(a, b))) = q(graphPoint(a, 0)); (L6) infDist(q(graphPoint(a, b)), T_0) = |b|; (L7) finrank T_0 = n; (L8) for all m, k and continuous linear M, N : R^m -> R^k, with hsNormSq M = sum_{i<m} |M e_i|^2 (standard basis) and hsNorm M = sqrt(hsNormSq M): (a) 0 <= hsNormSq M, (b) hsNorm(M)^2 = hsNormSq M, (c) hsNormSq(M + N) <= 2 hsNormSq M + 2 hsNormSq N, (d) hsNormSq(-M) = hsNormSq M, (e) hsNormSq M = 0 implies M = 0, (f) ||M|| <= hsNorm M, (g) hsNorm M <= sqrt(m) ||M|| (||.|| the operator norm); (L9) for every m and every linear subspace K of R^m, hsNormSq(K.starProjection) <= m.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ), (∀ (a a' : Rn n) (b b' : Rn ℓ), graphPoint (a + a') (b + b') = graphPoint a b + graphPoint a' b') ∧ (∀ (a a' : Rn n) (b b' : Rn ℓ), graphPoint (a - a') (b - b') = graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), graphPoint (t • a) (t • b) = t • graphPoint a b) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), ‖graphPoint a b‖ ^ 2 = ‖a‖ ^ 2 + ‖b‖ ^ 2) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), (rotatedPlane q).starProjection (q (graphPoint a b)) = q (graphPoint a (0 : Rn ℓ))) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), infDist (q (graphPoint a b)) (rotatedPlane q : Set (Amb n ℓ)) = ‖b‖) ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (rotatedPlane q) = n ∧ (∀ (m k : ℕ) (M N : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k), 0 ≤ hsNormSq M ∧ hsNorm M ^ 2 = hsNormSq M ∧ hsNormSq (M + N) ≤ 2 * hsNormSq M + 2 * hsNormSq N ∧ hsNormSq (-M) = hsNormSq M ∧ (hsNormSq M = 0 → M = 0) ∧ ‖M‖ ≤ hsNorm M ∧ hsNorm M ≤ Real.sqrt m * ‖M‖) ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule ℝ (Rn m)), hsNormSq K.starProjection ≤ m
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. N := n + l. For k in Fin N let eps_k be the k-th standard basis vector of R^N = Amb n l; e_i (i < n), f_j (j < l) are the standard basis vectors of R^n, R^l. Every index of Fin N is exactly one of castAdd l i (i < n) or natAdd n j (j < l). By definition graphPoint a b = toLp(Fin.append a b), i.e. (graphPoint a b)_{castAdd l i} = a_i and (graphPoint a b)_{natAdd n j} = b_j. hsNormSq M = sum_{i<m} |M e_i|^2, hsNorm M = sqrt(hsNormSq M), ||.|| is the operator norm, T_0 := rotatedPlane q = q(horizontalPlane).

1. (L1)-(L3). Compare coordinates. At castAdd l i both sides of (L1) equal a_i + a'_i and at natAdd n j both equal b_j + b'_j; likewise (L2) with differences and (L3) with t a_i and t b_j. Vectors of R^N with equal coordinates are equal.

2. (L4) and inner products. Splitting the sum over Fin N into its castAdd and natAdd parts (Fin.sum_univ_add): |graphPoint a b|^2 = sum_k (graphPoint a b)_k^2 = sum_{i<n} a_i^2 + sum_{j<l} b_j^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2. The same splitting gives <graphPoint a b, graphPoint a' b'> = <a, a'> + <b, b'>.

3. Description of horizontalPlane. By step 1 (coordinates), eps_{castAdd l i} = graphPoint(e_i, 0), so by (L1), (L3) graphPoint(a, 0) = sum_i a_i eps_{castAdd l i} lies in horizontalPlane; conversely every element sum_i c_i eps_{castAdd l i} of the span equals graphPoint(sum_i c_i e_i, 0). Hence horizontalPlane = {graphPoint(c, 0) : c in R^n}. For h = graphPoint(c, 0) and any b, step 2 gives <graphPoint(0, b), h> = <0, c> + <b, 0> = 0.

4. (L5). Let v := q(graphPoint a b) and k := q(graphPoint a 0). By step 3, k lies in q(horizontalPlane) = T_0. By (L2) and linearity of q, v - k = q(graphPoint(a - a, b - 0)) = q(graphPoint(0, b)). Every element of T_0 is q(h) with h in horizontalPlane, and <q(graphPoint(0, b)), q(h)> = <graphPoint(0, b), h> = 0, because the linear isometry q preserves inner products (polarization) and by step 3. Thus k is in T_0 and v - k is orthogonal to T_0. T_0 is finite-dimensional, hence complete, and the orthogonal projection onto a complete subspace K is characterized by: if k in K and <v - k, w> = 0 for all w in K, then P_K v = k. Hence P_{T_0} v = k = q(graphPoint(a, 0)).

5. (L6). Let K be a complete subspace, P := P_K and v a vector. For k in K, v - Pv is orthogonal to K and Pv - k lies in K, so by Pythagoras |v - k|^2 = |v - Pv|^2 + |Pv - k|^2 >= |v - Pv|^2; and Pv lies in K. Hence infDist(v, K) = inf_{k in K} |v - k| = |v - Pv|. With K = T_0 and v = q(graphPoint a b), step 4 gives v - Pv = q(graphPoint(0, b)), whose norm is |graphPoint(0, b)| = (|0|^2 + |b|^2)^(1/2) = |b| by (L4) and since q is an isometry.

6. (L7). The n vectors eps_{castAdd l i}, i < n, are distinct members of the standard orthonormal basis (castAdd l is injective), hence linearly independent, so their span horizontalPlane has finrank n. T_0 is the image of horizontalPlane under the linear equivalence q, and the image of a subspace under a linear equivalence has the same finrank. So finrank T_0 = n.

7. (L8). Let M, N : R^m -> R^k be linear and e_i (i < m) the standard basis.
(a), (b): hsNormSq M is a finite sum of squares, so it is >= 0, and hsNorm(M)^2 = (sqrt(hsNormSq M))^2 = hsNormSq M.
(c): for each i, |(M+N)e_i| <= |M e_i| + |N e_i| and (x + y)^2 <= 2x^2 + 2y^2 (since 2x^2 + 2y^2 - (x+y)^2 = (x - y)^2 >= 0), so |(M+N)e_i|^2 <= 2|M e_i|^2 + 2|N e_i|^2; sum over i.
(d): |(-M)e_i| = |-(M e_i)| = |M e_i|.
(e): if hsNormSq M = 0, every summand (each >= 0) is 0, so M e_i = 0 for all i; every v in R^m is sum_i v_i e_i, so M v = sum_i v_i M e_i = 0, i.e. M = 0.
(f): for v = sum_i v_i e_i, |M v| <= sum_i |v_i| |M e_i| <= (sum_i v_i^2)^(1/2) (sum_i |M e_i|^2)^(1/2) = |v| hsNorm M (triangle inequality, then Cauchy-Schwarz in R^m). Since hsNorm M >= 0, the definition of the operator norm gives ||M|| <= hsNorm M.
(g): |M e_i| <= ||M|| |e_i| = ||M||, so hsNormSq M <= m ||M||^2, and taking (monotone) square roots, hsNorm M <= sqrt(m ||M||^2) = sqrt(m) ||M||.

8. (L9). K is finite-dimensional, hence complete, and v = P_K v + (v - P_K v) with orthogonal summands, so |P_K v|^2 <= |v|^2. Hence hsNormSq(P_K) = sum_{i<m} |P_K e_i|^2 <= sum_{i<m} |e_i|^2 = m.
proof_key_steps: Coordinates of graphPoint (castAdd part a, natAdd part b) give (L1)-(L3), |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2 and the inner-product splitting

horizontalPlane = {graphPoint(c,0)} and graphPoint(0,b) is orthogonal to it; q preserves inner products, so P_{T_0} q(graphPoint(a,b)) = q(graphPoint(a,0)) by the characterization of orthogonal projections
Pythagoras gives infDist(v,K) = |v - P_K v|, which equals |b| for v = q(graphPoint(a,b))
T_0 is the image under the linear equivalence q of the span of n orthonormal vectors, so finrank T_0 = n
Hilbert-Schmidt facts termwise; Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||M|| <= hsNorm M; |M e_i| <= ||M|| gives hsNorm M <= sqrt(m)||M||; |P_K e_i| <= 1 gives hsNormSq(P_K) <= m

subproblem.title: Scaled L^p norm of H on sub-balls: monotonicity and the Hoelder bound for the L^1 norm
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (z : Amb n ℓ) (r ρ : ℝ), 0 < r → r ≤ ρ → closedBall z r ⊆ closedBall 0 ρ → V.scaledLpNorm H p z r ≤ V.scaledLpNorm H p 0 ρ ∧ ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 ≤ δ → V.scaledLpNorm H p 0 ρ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ → V.weight (closedBall z r) < ⊤ → ∫ x in closedBall z r, ‖H x‖ ∂V.weight ≤ δ * ρ ^ ((n : ℝ) / p - 1) * (V.weight (closedBall z r)).toReal ^ (1 - 1 / p)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. mu := V.weight; B := closedBall z r; ‖H x‖ₑ is the extended norm of H(x), so ‖H x‖ₑ = ofReal(‖H x‖). For xi in R^(n+l) and real sigma, I(xi, sigma) := lower integral over closedBall xi sigma of ‖H x‖ₑ^p d mu, a value in [0, infinity]; so K(xi, sigma) = (ofReal(sigma^(p-n)) * I(xi, sigma))^(1/p). Let f : R^(n+l) -> R, f(x) := ‖H x‖ (the real norm of H(x)). Then f >= 0 everywhere and ofReal(f(x)) = ‖H x‖ₑ for every x. Nothing is assumed or used about the measurability or integrability of H itself: every measure-theoretic property invoked below is a property of the real function f.

1. Since n >= 1 and p > n: p > 1, p - n > 0 and 0 < 1/p < 1. Also rho >= r > 0.

2. (K1).
- t -> t^(p-n) is nondecreasing on [0, infinity) (positive exponent), so r^(p-n) <= rho^(p-n) and ofReal(r^(p-n)) <= ofReal(rho^(p-n)) (Real.rpow_le_rpow, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal).
- B is contained in closedBall 0 rho, so I(z, r) <= I(0, rho): the lower integral of an arbitrary [0, infinity]-valued function is monotone in the domain (mu restricted to B is <= mu restricted to closedBall 0 rho), with no measurability needed (lintegral_mono_set).
- Multiplication on [0, infinity] is monotone in each factor, and t -> t^(1/p) is nondecreasing on [0, infinity] (1/p >= 0; ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow).
Hence K(z, r) = (ofReal(r^(p-n)) I(z, r))^(1/p) <= (ofReal(rho^(p-n)) I(0, rho))^(1/p) = K(0, rho).

3. (K2): set-up and case split on the integrability of f. Let delta >= 0 with K(0, rho) <= ofReal(delta) and mu(B) < infinity. Put RHS := delta * rho^(n/p - 1) * (mu(B).toReal)^(1 - 1/p). Then RHS >= 0: delta >= 0, rho^(n/p - 1) > 0 because rho > 0, and (mu(B).toReal)^(1 - 1/p) >= 0 as a real power of the nonnegative real mu(B).toReal. The integral in (K2) is the Bochner integral over B of the real-valued function f = ‖H‖. Let nu := mu restricted to B. Split on whether f is integrable on B with respect to mu (IntegrableOn f B mu, i.e. f is nu-integrable).
Case A: f is not integrable on B. The Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0 by convention (integral_undef, applied to the function f and the measure nu). Hence the integral over B of ‖H x‖ d mu equals 0 <= RHS, and (K2) holds.
Case B: f is integrable on B. Integrability of f with respect to nu includes the nu-a.e. strong measurability of f; hence f is nu-a.e. measurable, and so is x -> ofReal(f(x)) = ‖H x‖ₑ (composition of the measurable map ofReal with f; IntegrableOn f B mu unfolds to Integrable f nu, then Integrable.aestronglyMeasurable and ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp_aemeasurable). Steps 4-6 treat Case B and use only these properties of f.

4. Bound on I(z, r)^(1/p) (valid in both cases).
- On [0, infinity], (a b)^(1/p) = a^(1/p) b^(1/p) since 1/p >= 0 (ENNReal.mul_rpow_of_nonneg).
- Since rho > 0, ofReal(rho^(p-n))^(1/p) = ofReal((rho^(p-n))^(1/p)) = ofReal(rho^((p-n)/p)) (ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg, Real.rpow_mul).
- So K(0, rho) = ofReal(c) I(0, rho)^(1/p) with c := rho^((p-n)/p), and 0 < c < infinity; by hypothesis ofReal(c) I(0, rho)^(1/p) <= ofReal(delta).
- ofReal(c) is neither 0 nor infinity, so dividing by it: I(0, rho)^(1/p) <= ofReal(delta)/ofReal(c) = ofReal(delta/c) = ofReal(delta rho^(-(p-n)/p)) = ofReal(delta rho^(n/p - 1)), since -(p-n)/p = n/p - 1 (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le, ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos, Real.rpow_neg).
- By step 2, I(z, r) <= I(0, rho), and t -> t^(1/p) is monotone, so I(z, r)^(1/p) <= ofReal(delta rho^(n/p - 1)).

5. Hoelder (Case B).
- Let q' := p/(p-1). Then p, q' > 1 are Hoelder conjugate (1/p + 1/q' = 1; Real.HolderConjugate.conjExponent) and 1/q' = 1 - 1/p.

subproblem.title: Translation invariance of ball masses, tilt-excess, scaled L^p norms and the multiplicity condition
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U U' : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (V' : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U') (ζ : Amb n ℓ), V'.weight = V.weight.map (fun x => x - ζ) → (∀ x, V'.mult x = V.mult (ζ + x)) → (∀ x, V'.tangentProj x = V.tangentProj (ζ + x)) → (∀ s : ℝ, V'.weight (closedBall 0 s) = V.weight (closedBall ζ s)) ∧ (∀ (s : ℝ) (T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), V'.tiltExcess 0 s T = V.tiltExcess ζ s T) ∧ (∀ (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (p s : ℝ), V'.scaledLpNorm (fun x => H (ζ + x)) p 0 s = V.scaledLpNorm H p ζ s) ∧ ((∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, 1 ≤ V.mult x) → ∀ᵐ x ∂V'.weight, 1 ≤ V'.mult x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. mu := V.weight, mu' := V'.weight = tau_# mu with tau(x) := x - zeta.

1. Change of variables. tau is a bijection of R^(n+l) with inverse x -> zeta + x, and both maps are continuous. So tau is a measurable equivalence for the Borel sigma-algebra (Mathlib's MeasurableEquiv.subRight). For a measurable equivalence, every set S (measurable or not) satisfies:
(a) tau_# mu(S) = mu(tau^(-1)(S));
(b) (tau_# mu) restricted to S equals tau_#(mu restricted to tau^(-1)(S));
(c) for every measure nu and every function phi, lower integral of phi d(tau_# nu) = lower integral of phi o tau d nu, and likewise for Bochner integrals. No measurability or integrability assumptions are needed along a measurable equivalence.
Combining (b) and (c): the integral of phi over S w.r.t. mu' equals the integral of phi o tau over tau^(-1)(S) w.r.t. mu, for both lower and Bochner integrals.

2. tau^(-1)(B_s(0)) = {y : |y - zeta| <= s} = B_s(zeta) for every real s (both empty for s < 0).

3. (R1). mu'(B_s(0)) = mu(tau^(-1) B_s(0)) = mu(B_s(zeta)) by 1(a) and 2.

4. (R2). By definition and the hypothesis on V'.tangentProj, V'.tiltExcess 0 s T = (s^n)^(-1) times the Bochner integral over B_s(0) of phi d mu', where phi(x) := hsNormSq(V.tangentProj(zeta + x) - P_T). By steps 1 and 2 this equals (s^n)^(-1) times the integral over B_s(zeta) of phi(tau(y)) d mu(y). Since zeta + (y - zeta) = y, phi(tau(y)) = hsNormSq(V.tangentProj y - P_T). Hence V'.tiltExcess 0 s T = (s^n)^(-1) integral_{B_s(zeta)} hsNormSq(V.tangentProj y - P_T) d mu = V.tiltExcess zeta s T.

5. (R3). V'.scaledLpNorm (H(zeta + .)) p 0 s = (ofReal(s^(p-n)) * lower integral over B_s(0) of |H(zeta + x)|^p d mu'(x))^(1/p). By steps 1 and 2, the lower integral equals the lower integral over B_s(zeta) of |H(zeta + (y - zeta))|^p d mu(y), i.e. over B_s(zeta) of |H(y)|^p d mu(y). The prefactor ofReal(s^(p-n)) and the exponent 1/p are the same for V and V', both n-dimensional. So the two scaled L^p norms are equal.

6. (R4). Let Z := {x : not (1 <= V'.mult x)}. Since V'.mult x = V.mult(zeta + x), tau^(-1)(Z) = {y : not (1 <= V.mult(zeta + (y - zeta)))} = {y : not (1 <= V.mult y)}, which is mu-null by assumption. By 1(a), mu'(Z) = mu(tau^(-1) Z) = 0, i.e. 1 <= V'.mult x for mu'-a.e. x.
proof_key_steps: tau(x) = x - zeta is a measurable equivalence; push-forward evaluation and change of variables hold for all sets and functions
tau^(-1)(B_s(0)) = B_s(zeta)
(R1)-(R3) by change of variables and zeta + (y - zeta) = y
(R4): tau^(-1){V'.mult < 1} = {V.mult < 1}, which is mu-null

subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. A, B : R^n -> R^l are linear. W_A : R^n -> R^(n+l), W_A v := q(graphPoint(v, A v)). G_A, P_A, P_0 are as in the statement. |X| := hsNorm X, so |X|^2 = hsNormSq X by (L8b); ||.|| is the operator norm. (L1)-(L9) are the conclusions of la_basics.

0. Preliminaries.
(i) W_A is linear: W_A(v + v') = q(graphPoint(v + v', A v + A v')) = W_A v + W_A v' by (L1) and linearity of q, and W_A(t v) = t W_A v by (L3).
(ii) v -> graphPoint(v, A v) is linear (same reasons), so its range is a linear subspace and equals its own span. Applying q: G_A = {W_A v : v in R^n}.
(iii) |W_A v|^2 = |graphPoint(v, A v)|^2 = |v|^2 + |A v|^2 <= (1 + ||A||^2)|v|^2 (q is an isometry; (L4)). Hence ||W_A||^2 <= 1 + ||A||^2.
(iv) By (L2) and linearity of q, W_A v - W_B v = q(graphPoint(0, (A - B)v)).

1. (P1). q(graphPoint(x, A x)) = W_A x lies in G_A, and an orthogonal projection fixes every vector of its range.

|w| <= |w - A v| + |A v| <= 1*|w - A v| + ||A||*|v| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) (|w - A v|^2 + |v|^2)^(1/2) = (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) |y - P_A y|,
where the third inequality is Cauchy-Schwarz in R^2.

3. (P3) (Ang). Let v in R^n and e := W_A v. By (P1), P_A e = e. By (L5) with (a, b) = (v, A v), P_0 e = q(graphPoint(v, 0)). Hence (P_A - P_0)e = q(graphPoint(v, A v)) - q(graphPoint(v, 0)) = q(graphPoint(0, A v)) by (L2), and its norm is |A v| by (L4). Therefore
|A v| <= ||P_A - P_0|| |e| <= ||P_A - P_0|| (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) |v| by 0(iii).
This holds for all v and the constant (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) ||P_A - P_0|| is >= 0, so the definition of the operator norm gives ||A|| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) ||P_A - P_0||.

(HS2) For linear Y : R^k -> R^p: |Y X|^2 = sum_i |Y(X e_i)|^2 <= ||Y||^2 sum_i |X e_i|^2 = ||Y||^2 |X|^2.
(HS3) For linear W : R^p -> R^m: |X W|^2 <= ||W||^2 |X|^2. Indeed (X W)* = W* X* and ||W*|| = ||W||, so by (HS1), (HS2), (HS1): |X W|^2 = |W* X*|^2 <= ||W*||^2 |X*|^2 = ||W||^2 |X|^2.
(HS4) For linear X : R^N -> R^N (N = n + l) and an orthogonal projection P of R^N: |X|^2 = |X P|^2 + |X(I - P)|^2. P and I - P are self-adjoint, so by (HS1) |X P|^2 = |P X*|^2 and |X(I - P)|^2 = |(I - P) X*|^2. For every u, P u is orthogonal to (I - P)u, so |P u|^2 + |(I - P)u|^2 = |u|^2. Take u = X* f_j, sum over j and use (HS1): |P X*|^2 + |(I - P)X*|^2 = |X*|^2 = |X|^2.

subproblem.title: Integrability, lower-integral form, radius monotonicity and nonnegativity of the tilt-excess integral
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight → ∀ (ζ : Amb n ℓ) (T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → V.weight (closedBall ζ s) < ⊤ → ∫⁻ y in closedBall ζ s, ENNReal.ofReal (hsNormSq (V.tangentProj y - T.starProjection)) ∂V.weight = ENNReal.ofReal (s ^ n * V.tiltExcess ζ s T)) ∧ (∀ σ s : ℝ, 0 < σ → σ ≤ s → V.weight (closedBall ζ s) < ⊤ → σ ^ n * V.tiltExcess ζ σ T ≤ s ^ n * V.tiltExcess ζ s T) ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → 0 ≤ V.tiltExcess ζ s T

Notation. mu := V.weight, p_y := V.tangentProj y, P_T := T.starProjection, f(y) := hsNormSq(p_y - P_T), B_s := closedBall zeta s, E(s) := V.tiltExcess zeta s T = (s^n)^(-1) * (Bochner integral of f over B_s). (L8), (L9) are from la_basics.

1. Uniform bound. By the definition of tangentProj, for every y either p_y = K.starProjection for some linear subspace K of R^(n+l) (the chosen approximate tangent space) or p_y = 0. In the first case hsNormSq(p_y) <= n + l by (L9) with m = n + l; in the second, hsNormSq(p_y) = 0. Also hsNormSq(P_T) <= n + l by (L9), so hsNormSq(-P_T) <= n + l by (L8d). By (L8c) with M = p_y and N = -P_T, and by (L8a): 0 <= f(y) <= 2(n + l) + 2(n + l) = 4(n + l) for every y.

2. A.e. strong measurability. Phi : M -> hsNormSq(M - P_T), on the finite-dimensional normed space of continuous linear maps of R^(n+l), is continuous: it is a finite sum of squares of norms of the continuous maps M -> (M - P_T)e_i. Since y -> p_y is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, so is f = Phi o p, with respect to mu and to every restriction of mu.

3. Integrability. If mu(B_s) < infinity, then f is a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by 4(n + l) on B_s, a set of finite measure. So f is mu-integrable on B_s.

4. (T1). Let s > 0 with mu(B_s) < infinity. By step 3 and f >= 0, the identity for nonnegative integrable functions gives ofReal(integral_{B_s} f d mu) = lower integral over B_s of ofReal(f) d mu. Since s > 0, s^n > 0, so s^n E(s) = s^n (s^n)^(-1) integral_{B_s} f d mu = integral_{B_s} f d mu. Hence the lower integral equals ofReal(s^n E(s)).

5. (T2). Let 0 < sigma <= s with mu(B_s) < infinity. As in step 4, sigma^n E(sigma) = integral_{B_sigma} f d mu and s^n E(s) = integral_{B_s} f d mu. Now B_sigma is contained in B_s, f is integrable on B_s (step 3) and f >= 0. Monotonicity of set integrals of nonnegative integrable functions in the domain gives integral_{B_sigma} f d mu <= integral_{B_s} f d mu.

6. (T3). For s > 0, (s^n)^(-1) > 0. Also integral_{B_s} f d mu >= 0 because f >= 0 everywhere; a Bochner integral of a nonnegative function is nonnegative, and it is 0 when the function is not integrable. Hence E(s) >= 0.

f is a continuous function of the a.e. strongly measurable tangentProj, hence integrable on balls of finite measure
(T1): ofReal of the integral of a nonnegative integrable function is its lower integral; s^n (s^n)^(-1) = 1
(T2): monotonicity of set integrals of nonnegative integrable functions in the domain

0. If R <= 0 then Omega is empty and the left side is 0. Assume R > 0, so 0 lies in Omega.

1. Borel representative. Since y -> p_y is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, there is a strongly measurable map p~ : R^(n+l) -> L(R^(n+l), R^(n+l)) with p~_y = p_y for mu-a.e. y. p~ is Borel measurable, because a strongly measurable map into this finite-dimensional normed space is Borel. The set {y : p_y != p~_y} is mu-null, so it is contained in a Borel set N' with mu(N') = 0 (a measurable hull).

subproblem.title: Identification of the tangent projection at a Lebesgue point with a plane of vanishing tilt-excess
subproblem.statement:
Let n, l >= 0, U any set, and V a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U with weight mu such that y -> p_y := V.tangentProj y is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. Let zeta in R^(n+l), S a linear subspace with orthogonal projection P_S, and c > 0, s_0 > 0 with ofReal(c s^n) <= mu(B_s(zeta)) < infinity for all s in (0, s_0] (closed balls). Assume:
(L) mu(B_s(zeta))^(-1) * (lower integral over B_s(zeta) of ofReal(hsNormSq(p_y - p_zeta)) d mu(y)) -> 0 as s -> 0+;
(T) V.tiltExcess zeta s S -> 0 as s -> 0+.
Then V.tangentProj zeta = P_S.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight → ∀ (ζ : Amb n ℓ) (S : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)) (c s₀ : ℝ), 0 < c → 0 < s₀ → (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ s₀ → ENNReal.ofReal (c * s ^ n) ≤ V.weight (closedBall ζ s) ∧ V.weight (closedBall ζ s) < ⊤) → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => (V.weight (closedBall ζ s))⁻¹ * ∫⁻ y in closedBall ζ s, ENNReal.ofReal (hsNormSq (V.tangentProj y - V.tangentProj ζ)) ∂V.weight) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => V.tiltExcess ζ s S) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → V.tangentProj ζ = S.starProjection
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- mu := V.weight, p_y := V.tangentProj y, P_S := S.starProjection, B_s := closedBall zeta s, m_s := mu(B_s), E_s := V.tiltExcess zeta s S.
- a(y) := ofReal(hsNormSq(p_y - p_zeta)) and b(y) := ofReal(hsNormSq(p_y - P_S)).
- Avg_s := m_s^(-1) times the lower integral of a over B_s; this is the quantity in (L).
- (L8) is from la_basics and (T1) from tilt_integrals.

1. Pointwise inequality. D := hsNormSq(p_zeta - P_S) >= 0 by (L8a). For every y, p_zeta - P_S = (-(p_y - p_zeta)) + (p_y - P_S). By (L8c) and (L8d), D <= 2 hsNormSq(p_y - p_zeta) + 2 hsNormSq(p_y - P_S). ofReal is monotone, and ofReal(2s + 2t) = 2 ofReal(s) + 2 ofReal(t) for s, t >= 0. So ofReal(D) <= 2 a(y) + 2 b(y) for every y.

2. Measurability. M -> ofReal(hsNormSq(M - C)) is continuous for fixed C, and y -> p_y is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. So a and b are mu-a.e. measurable.

3. Estimate at a fixed scale. Let 0 < s <= s_0. By hypothesis 0 < ofReal(c s^n) <= m_s < infinity (c > 0, s > 0).
- Integrate step 1 over B_s. The lower integral of a constant is the constant times the measure; the lower integral is additive when one summand is a.e.-measurable; constants factor out. This gives ofReal(D) m_s <= 2 integral_{B_s} a d mu + 2 integral_{B_s} b d mu.
- By (T1) with T = S (using s > 0, m_s < infinity and the a.e. strong measurability of p): integral_{B_s} b d mu = ofReal(s^n E_s).
- Multiply by m_s^(-1); since m_s is in (0, infinity), m_s m_s^(-1) = 1. So ofReal(D) <= 2 Avg_s + 2 m_s^(-1) ofReal(s^n E_s).
- From ofReal(c s^n) <= m_s: m_s^(-1) <= ofReal(c s^n)^(-1) = ofReal((c s^n)^(-1)). Hence m_s^(-1) ofReal(s^n E_s) <= ofReal((c s^n)^(-1)) ofReal(s^n E_s) = ofReal((c s^n)^(-1) s^n E_s) = ofReal(E_s/c).
So for every s in (0, s_0]:
(*) ofReal(D) <= 2 Avg_s + 2 ofReal(E_s/c).

4. Passage to the limit. Let s -> 0+ along the filter of right neighbourhoods of 0.
- Avg_s -> 0 by (L).
- E_s -> 0 by (T); hence E_s/c -> 0 and, by continuity of ofReal, ofReal(E_s/c) -> 0.
- Multiplication by the finite constant 2 and addition are continuous at these finite limits in [0, infinity], so the right side of (*) tends to 0.
(0, s_0] belongs to this filter, so (*) holds eventually, and the filter is nontrivial. Therefore ofReal(D) <= 0, so ofReal(D) = 0 and D <= 0. With D >= 0, D = 0.

5. Conclusion. By (L8e), hsNormSq(p_zeta - P_S) = 0 implies p_zeta - P_S = 0, i.e. V.tangentProj zeta = S.starProjection.
